jobs.description:
Be Part of Our Next Chapter

For over almost 60 years, our solutions have enabled impactful connections between some of the world’s leading brands and their customers. And while we’ve already done a lot of work we’re proud of, we’re just getting started!

We’re a global technology company focused on creating dynamic, smart, personalized and engaging customer experiences powered by our range of digital hardware, our proprietary content management system and our industry leading signage solutions. (For example: If you’ve ordered in-store or in the drive-thru at McDonald’s somewhere in the world in the last few years, chances are you’ve interacted with our digital solutions.) We work in over 50 global markets and have 9 offices around the world, with a global headquarters proudly located in our founding home of Sydney, Australia.

Coates Group has the values of a family-owned business and the innovative spirit of a start-up, both which fuel our purpose – Creating Connections. Empowering Partnerships. Always Evolving . Through hard work, dedication and creativity, we’ve become industry leaders who have won awards and set records while remaining focused on continual growth and evolution. We are a 2x Australia Good Design Award winner and successfully completed the largest hardware deployment in Quick Service Restaurant history.

We are curious, charismatic, authentic and we value and leverage the diversity of our crew. We are imaginers, kindness enthusiasts, experts, creators, thinkers, challengers, collaborators and over-achievers. And together, as a Crew, we are revolutionizing the way the world’s leading brands leverage technology to drive the best customer experiences.

The Director, Engineering
is accountable for enabling high-performing engineering squads to deliver reliable, maintainable, and high-quality software solutions. This role provides technical leadership, builds capability across engineers and technical leads, ensures adherence to engineering standards, and removes blockers that impede delivery, while partnering with Product, Delivery, and QA leadership to achieve business and customer outcomes.

Responsibilities

Engineering Enablement: Ensure squads have the technical capability, processes, and practices to deliver reliably, removing engineering blockers and supporting predictable outcomes in partnership with Delivery leadership.
Engineering Leadership & Capability: Act as a chapter-style leader for engineers and technical leads, building capability, setting standards, and driving consistent engineering practices across squads.
Technical Leadership, Debt & Design Quality: Ensure sound technical design and implementation, actively managing technical debt and addressing complexity.
Quality in Delivery: Embed quality-by-design within engineering teams (e.g. testability, code quality, CI/CD discipline), while partnering with QA to achieve agreed quality outcomes.
Platform Health & Operability: Own the operational health of systems within scope, ensuring reliability, performance, and readiness across production and pre-production environments.
People & Partner Leadership: Lead and develop permanent and partner engineers (onshore and offshore), including performance management, engagement, and effective integration.
Delivery Flow & Dependencies: Enable squads to operate autonomously by removing engineering blockers, managing dependencies, and improving delivery flow in partnership with Product and Delivery.

Capabilities

Hands-on Technical Leadership: Leads with strong engineering credibility and modelling high-quality full-stack engineering practices.
Execution Focus: Translates architectural direction and standards into practical, repeatable engineering practices that work at squad level.
Problem Solving & Judgement: Quickly diagnoses technical and delivery-adjacent issues, makes sound trade-offs, and removes engineering blockers.
People Development: Develops a high-performing team through clear expectations, feedback, and career coaching.
Collaboration & Influence: Works as a trusted partner to Product, Delivery & QA leaders to align engineering effort to shared outcomes.
Ownership & Accountability: Builds strong ownership within squads for code quality, operability, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications

8+ years’ experience in software engineering, with 3+ years in an engineering leadership roles, managing engineers and technical leads
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience
Proven experience delivering enterprise-scale software platforms or digital products within complex, client environments
Strong hands-on background in modern full-stack software engineering, with deep experience in building highly scalable web applications supported by cloud-native or serverless architectures (AWS preferred), CI/CD pipelines, and distributed systems
Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional engineering teams operating in agile or product-led delivery models
Experience establishing and enforcing engineering standards, development practices, and delivery discipline across multiple squads
Proven ability to manage a blended workforce, including permanent staff and staff-augmented delivery partners (onshore and offshore)
Demonstrated experience in developing and executing plans that align with business objectives and growth

$190,000 - $210,000 a year

We are industry leaders who have won awards and set records. We are a 2x Australia Good Design Award winner and we successfully completed the largest hardware deployment in Quick Service Restaurant history.

We are led by a forward-thinking CEO who has demonstrated a true passion for people and making Coates a place where people genuinely enjoy working. Our growth plans enable a focus on providing rapid career advancement opportunities for our talent.

Together, we are creators, allowing us to make our purpose a reality – to create immersive brand experiences for everyone.

Join a Crew that Cares

Be part of a global team of talented, ambitious, creative people that value integrity, individuality and inclusivity. (Ask us about our Equality + Empowerment Initiatives).

The benefits include an annual market competitive bonus program and our “Thrive Program” which includes a suite of flexible work options because we’re strong believers that you should never miss an important life or work moment. Thrive also provides dedicated time to prioritize our health and wellbeing (think virtual Yoga or meditation sessions), a Global Wellness paid day off to recharge as well as a “Give Back Day” to allow our Crew an opportunity to make an impact in the community.

Be inspired To Be More

We skip the red tape and aim to always stay nimble. We’re proud of where we’ve been and are energized by where we’re going. We encourage ideas and perspectives because we know the more we have, the better we are. We work hard but have fun along the way. We push the boundaries but keep it real and authentic. We believe in the values that got us here are the ones that will continue to lead us forward. We are excited by what we’ve accomplished, but know the best is yet to come.

Position Summary...

What you'll do...The Director, Implementation – Automation & Infrastructure is responsible for leading a portfolio of complex automation, material handling, and industrial racking projects across multiple sites. The Director will lead a team of Site Implementation Managers, establishing consistent execution standards and ensuring projects are delivered safely, to scope, on schedule, within budget, and at the required operational performance. The Director will provide portfolio-level leadership from site readiness through installation, commissioning, go-live, and operational handoff. This role is accountable for proactively identifying systemic risks, resolving cross-functional constraints, managing strategic vendor performance, and ensuring project teams have the resources and support required to successfully execute. The role will leverage AI, data, and digital tools to improve portfolio visibility, identify emerging risks and trends, strengthen project controls, and enable faster, data-driven decisions across the implementation portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Leadership: Lead execution across a portfolio of concurrent automation, material handling, and industrial racking projects, ensuring consistent delivery against safety, scope, schedule, budget, quality, and operational readiness commitments.
Team Leadership: Lead, develop, and coach a team of Site Implementation Managers responsible for day-to-day field execution. Establish clear expectations, operating mechanisms, accountability, and development plans while ensuring appropriate resources are aligned to project needs.
Scope, Schedule & Budget: Maintain portfolio-level accountability for approved scope, project schedules, capital budgets, forecasts, and change control. Identify trends and variances across projects and ensure recovery plans are established when commitments are at risk.
Project Governance: Establish consistent project management standards, operating mechanisms, and performance reviews across the portfolio. Maintain clear visibility to scope, schedule, budget, risks, open issues, vendor performance, commissioning, and operational readiness.
Risk Management: Maintain portfolio-level visibility to project risk registers and proactively identify systemic and cross-project risks. Ensure mitigation plans, owners, and due dates are established and intervene when risks require senior leadership or cross-functional support.
Issue Resolution & Escalation: Provide leadership for critical issues that cannot be resolved at the project level. Remove organizational barriers, align decision-makers, and drive timely resolution of issues impacting project commitments.
Vendor & Partner Management: Provide leadership and governance for key equipment suppliers, system integrators, rack suppliers/installers, contractors, and engineering partners. Monitor performance across projects, identify systemic gaps, and hold partners accountable to contractual, schedule, quality, and performance commitments.
Cross-Functional Leadership: Partner with senior leaders across Engineering, Construction, Operations, Reliability/Maintenance, Technology, Safety, Procurement, Finance, and external partners to align priorities, resolve dependencies, and ensure successful project delivery.
Installation & Site Readiness: Ensure Site Implementation Managers have established comprehensive readiness plans covering site access, equipment delivery, staging, installation sequencing, utilities, construction interfaces, technology dependencies, and operational requirements.
Commissioning & Go-Live: Establish consistent expectations for testing, commissioning, acceptance testing, punch-list closure, performance validation, training, and operational readiness. Ensure projects meet defined acceptance criteria prior to transition into operations.
Change Management: Establish disciplined portfolio-level change control. Ensure proposed changes are evaluated for scope, cost, schedule, technical, and operational impacts and receive appropriate review and approval before execution.
AI & Digital Tools: Drive adoption of approved AI and digital project-management tools across the implementation organization to improve schedule and cost analysis, risk identification, issue management, document review, reporting, and identification of cross-project trends. Use AI-generated insights to strengthen decision-making while maintaining clear human accountability for project outcomes.
Operational Handoff: Ensure consistent standards are established for transition to Operations and Reliability, including documentation, training, spare parts, asset information, punch-list closure, open issues, system ownership, and post-go-live support.
Continuous Improvement: Capture lessons learned across projects and translate them into improved design standards, implementation processes, vendor expectations, commissioning practices, and future project requirements.

Head of Technology (USA)

About the Role 

Reporting to the GM - Technology, the purpose of the Head of Technology is to run Eco Outdoor's technology operations and delivery day to day, so our systems, vendors and projects keep pace with a business growing quickly across the US, Australia, and New Zealand.  
This role keeps our core platforms and partners (Salesforce, NetSuite, website and IT managed service providers) reliable and well supported, delivers technology projects on time and on budget, and builds a function that can scale shoulder-to-shoulder with the business. It also owns the technology in our offices and showrooms, and a repeatable model for fitting out new US locations.  
The Head of Technology partners closely with the GM Technology as a genuine deputy, and with leaders across Sales, Operations, Supply Chain, Marketing, People & Culture, Product, and Finance in both the US and Australia.  
The role is based in the United States ( on-site/hybrid, Los Angeles, CA
). The working schedule is 10:00am - 6:00pm (Pacific Time), Monday to Friday
. The later start is intended to give daily overlap with our Sydney team. The role includes occasional travel to Sydney and to our team in Semarang, Indonesia. 
Key Outputs  

Technology Operations and Managed Services

Keep our core business systems, Salesforce, NetSuite and our digital platforms, stable, secure and well supported across every region. 
Own day-to-day IT service across Australia and the US, delivered through our IT managed services partners, so our people get fast, reliable support wherever they work. 
Set and track service standards with each partner, with regular service reviews, so issues are resolved within SLAs and root causes are fixed rather than patched. 
Lead the evaluation of whether our managed services partners are fit to support the business's future growth, and drive the changes needed where they aren't. 

Workplace Technology

Make sure day-to-day physical technology works seamlessly across our offices and showrooms: AV, hardware and devices, office networking and wireless access points. 
Own the hardware lifecycle, from procurement and setup through to maintenance and replacement. 

Showroom and Site Buildouts

Partner with our Showroom Development and Construction Manager to support our physical growth across the US. 
Build a repeatable, documented technology model for new showrooms and sites, covering network, AV and hardware standards, suppliers, budgets and timelines. 
Make sure every new location opens technology-ready from day one, and refine the model with each build .  

Delivery

Run the technology project register and delivery cadence: scope, priority, timelines, budgets and status reporting. 
Make sure projects ship on time and to budget, with dependencies and risks surfaced early.  
Translate business needs from Sales, Operations, Supply Chain, Marketing, People & Culture, Product, and Finance into clear priorities, with structure and discipline around how new work is requested and signed off. 

Vendors, Partners and Procurement

Own our relationships with technology vendors and agencies in Australia and the US, leading procurement and contract renewals and holding them to agreed outcomes. 
Keep technology spend visible and within budget. 

Leadership and Deputy to the GM Technology

Lead a distributed team across the US, Australia and Indonesia, spanning systems engineering, systems administration and website, with working rhythms that make the most of our overlapping hours. 
Set clear priorities, coach and develop the team, and build a culture of ownership and follow-through. 
Represent technology in operational decisions, and step in for the GM Technology when needed. 
Be the senior, accountable, visible technology presence in our US business as it grows. 

Security, Governance and Continuous Improvement

Own day-to-day security across our systems, devices and networks, working with our managed services partners on access management, patching, backups and incident response, and reporting on cyber risk to the GM Technology. 
Maintain clear documentation and processes across our core systems. 
Work with our architecture and data leads so operational work supports our AI and automation roadmap. 

Skills and Experience 

8+ years' experience in technology operations, IT or business systems, including at least 3 years leading teams. 
Hands-on experience with Salesforce and/or NetSuite, whether in administration, integration or management. 
A proven track record delivering technology projects with strong delivery discipline, whether Agile, waterfall or a mix. 
Experience managing vendors, agencies and IT managed services providers, including negotiating contracts and scopes of work, and running a partner evaluation or transition. 
Working knowledge of physical IT infrastructure (networking, wireless, AV and end-user hardware) and cyber security frameworks such as NIST or CIS.
